title.narrative: SHF Improving Agricultural Production in BNS – SP FSL

description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtSamaritan’s Purse will implement an agricultural support program in South Al Kurmuk, targeting 2,000 vulnerable households (HHs) to enhance food security, build resilience, and promote sustainable agricultural practices. The program will prioritize internally displaced persons (IDPs), women-headed HHs, persons with disabilities (PWDs), and elderly individuals, addressing the pressing needs of conflict-affected communities.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThe primary source of livelihoods in Blue Nile State (BNS) is agriculture, practiced by over 80% of the population, according to the 2023 Post-Harvest Assessment (PHA) conducted in the region by Samaritan’s Purse. For a community to sustainably produce enough food to last from one season to the next, while maintaining adequate surplus to sell for income that meets HH needs, efforts must focus on improving agricultural practices and promoting modern technologies. These technologies will enable communities to achieve sufficient yields despite the global challenge of climate change.ltbrgtltbrgtThe program’s first outcome is to improve food security through the provision of essential agricultural inputs and capacity-building initiatives. Samaritan’s Purse will distribute 13 metric tons (MT) of open-pollinated sorghum seeds, enabling each HH to plant two feddans of land, along with 2,000 sets of farming tools (malodas/ hoes, rakes, and pangas). To reduce post-harvest losses, 3,714 hermetic seed bags and 2,200 tarpaulins (4x5 ft each) will also be distributed.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThe second outcome focuses on improving nutrition and income generation through the adoption of sustainable vegetable production and climate-smart agricultural practices. Samaritan’s Purse will train 2,000 HHs on topics such as integrated pest management (IPM), soil health management, and post-harvest storage techniques. Demonstration plots and farmer field schools will facilitate the practical application of these skills. Additionally, the cultivation of vegetables will be supported to diversify diets and generate additional income.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtBeneficiary selection will be guided by community engagement and transparency, ensuring that IDPs, vulnerable host community members, and other at-risk groups have equitable access to program resources. Criteria include demonstrated farming capacity, willingness to participate, and access to land facilitated by the Secretariat of Agriculture (SoA).lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtAligned with Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 2, this program integrates input distribution, training, and community collaboration to address immediate food security needs while fostering long-term resilience and sustainable agricultural practices in South Al Kurmuk, BNS. By equipping HHs with the tools and knowledge needed to adapt to challenges, the project will contribute to reducing food insecurity and enhancing community stability.ltbrgtlt/pgt
